supplement.where: No supplement or online appendix is referenced. Appendix A (mediation tables A1-A5) is inside this PDF, pp. 33-37.
supplement.holds: Nothing outside this PDF. Appendix A in the PDF holds regression coefficients with SEs, p-values and bias-corrected 95% CIs for the ChatGPT dummy, but only from mediation models that also condition on a mediator.

paper_design_summary: One hundred MTurk workers were randomly assigned to generate up to five new product ideas for a coffee mug with either a ChatGPT (GPT-3.5-turbo) interface or a Google Search interface; 10 failed attention checks, leaving 90 (45 per arm). The valid ideas were scored for count (productivity), ideas per second (efficiency), novelty and functional appropriateness rated by 300 MTurk raters, and divergence from other ideas in the same condition using text embeddings (divergent thinking).

studies.label: Online experiment: coffee-mug ideation with ChatGPT vs Google Search

assignment.what_was_assigned: Ideation tool built into the task interface: ChatGPT (GPT-3.5-turbo via OpenAI Chat Completion API) or Google Search (Custom Search JSON API)
assignment.quote: One hundred MTurk workers participated in the experiment. They were randomly assigned to either the LLM or the Search Engine condition and received U.S.$1.50 for participation.
assignment.locator: p. 11, Section 4 (Experimental Setup); also p. 9 'between-subjects design consisting of two conditions: LLM and search engine'

arms.name: LLM (ChatGPT)
arms.description: Interface with a ChatGPT panel (GPT-3.5-turbo, conversation memory, option to start a new conversation); had to send at least one message before the task page

arms.name: Search Engine (Google Search)
arms.description: Interface with a Google Custom Search panel; participants could browse result pages and open websites inside the interface; had to enter at least one query before the task page

participants.exclusions: 10 of 100 participants removed for failing attention checks in the post-task questionnaire (arm of the excluded not stated); final sample 90 (45 per arm). Idea-quality and divergent-thinking outcomes use only the 67 participants with at least one valid idea (39 LLM, 28 Search Engine); 450 submitted ideas were screened to 228 valid ideas (159 LLM, 69 Search Engine).
participants.who: MTurk workers with more than 5,000 approved tasks and an approval rate of at least 99%
participants.quote: Ten participants who failed attention checks were removed. Our final sample comprised 90 participants, with 45 for each tool.
participants.locator: p. 11, Section 4; Table 1 p. 12; Section 5.1 p. 12

ai_tool.name_model: ChatGPT via OpenAI Chat Completion API, GPT-3.5-turbo model
ai_tool.how_used: Free chat in a panel on the right side of the task interface; the model kept memory of recent prompts and responses; participants typed ideas into five boxes on the left; told not to use tools outside the interface.

task.description: Generate innovative ideas for a coffee mug, up to five ideas per participant
task.duration: not_stated (duration of stay on the interface was recorded but not reported)

outcomes.name: Idea Novelty
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: 300 MTurk raters (idea generators and attention-check failures excluded); each rated six random ideas on novel, original, exciting (7-point Likert); about 10.6 raters per idea; scores z-normalized within rater, averaged over the three items per idea, then averaged over each participant's valid ideas. Ideas were first summarized to 10 words or fewer by GPT-3.5-turbo to standardize writing style. Appendix Table A3 gives ChatGPT direct-effect coefficients conditional on each mediator.

contrasts.reported: Idea Novelty: LLM 0.010 (39) vs Search Engine -0.057 (28); Difference 0.018; F-statistic 4.88** (one-way ANOVA). Text: '0.010 vs. -0.057, p < 0.05'. Appendix A3 ChatGPT coefficient in mediation models: .1415462 (SE .0472364, p 0.004) with Information Volume; .0445833 (SE .0408076, p 0.280) with Information Relatedness; .1063616 (SE .0388696, p 0.009) with Information Divergency; .0783577 (SE .0328887, p 0.021) with Information Adoption.
contrasts.locator: p. 20, Table 3 Panel C; p. 19 text; p. 35, Table A3

outcomes.name: Functional Appropriateness
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Same MTurk rating procedure as Idea Novelty, items useful, effective, feasible; z-normalized within rater, averaged per idea, then per participant. Appendix Table A4 gives ChatGPT direct-effect coefficients conditional on each mediator.

contrasts.reported: Functional Appropriateness: LLM 0.055 (39) vs Search Engine 0.213 (28); Difference -0.159; F-statistic 10.77*** (one-way ANOVA). Text: '0.055 vs. 0.213, p < 0.01'. Appendix A4 ChatGPT coefficient in mediation models: -.2157089 (SE .0730666, p 0.005); -.1270472 (SE .0621546, p 0.047); -.1594458 (SE .0596584, p 0.010); -.1665013 (SE .0496893, p 0.002).
contrasts.locator: p. 20, Table 3 Panel C; p. 19 text; p. 36, Table A4

outcomes.name: Divergent Thinking (semantic divergence of ideas from other participants' ideas in the same condition)
outcomes.question: across_people
outcomes.measure_detail: For each idea, 1 minus the average cosine similarity between its text-embedding-ada-002 embedding and those of all other ideas from participants in the same condition; averaged over the participant's ideas. Footnote 10: TF-IDF embeddings give consistent results (not tabulated). Higher = more divergent, so no sign reversal. Appendix Table A5 gives ChatGPT direct-effect coefficients conditional on each mediator.

contrasts.reported: Divergent Thinking: LLM 0.134 (39) vs Search Engine 0.123 (28); Difference 0.011; F-statistic 25.68*** (one-way ANOVA). Text: 'participants in the LLM condition generated more diverse ideas than those in the Search Engine condition (0.134 vs. 0.123, p < 0.01)'. Appendix A5 ChatGPT coefficient in mediation models: .0107992 (SE .0038407, p 0.007); .0151029 (SE .0032118, p 0.000); .006888 (SE .0028358, p 0.019); .014556 (SE .0023706, p 0.000).
contrasts.locator: p. 20, Table 3 Panel C; p. 19 text; p. 37, Table A5

diversity_detail.metric: Idea divergence = 1 minus mean cosine similarity to other ideas in the same condition, averaged within participant
diversity_detail.computed_over: Each idea against all other ideas from participants within the same condition (the text does not say whether the participant's own other ideas are excluded); then averaged over each participant's ideas
diversity_detail.uncertainty: One-way ANOVA on participant-level scores (F-statistic with significance stars); no SDs or SEs for the arm difference in the main text
diversity_detail.notes: Computed on GPT-3.5-turbo summaries of the ideas (10 words or fewer), not the original text. Pools differ in size across arms (159 vs 69 valid ideas).

outcomes.name: Productivity (number of valid ideas)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Count of valid ideas per participant after two postgraduate students screened out off-topic, duplicate, and multi-idea entries (maximum 5). Participants with zero valid ideas count as 0. Appendix Table A1 gives mediation results.

contrasts.reported: Productivity: LLM 3.533 (45) vs Search Engine 1.533 (45); Difference 2.000; F-statistic 27.65*** (one-way ANOVA). Text: '3.533 vs. 1.533, p < 0.01'.
contrasts.locator: p. 20, Table 3 Panel C; p. 19 text; p. 33, Table A1

outcomes.name: Efficiency (valid ideas per second on the interface)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Number of valid ideas divided by the duration of the participant's stay on the interface (seconds). Speed of idea production, not a creativity rating. Appendix Table A2 gives mediation results.

contrasts.reported: Efficiency: LLM 0.010 (45) vs Search Engine 0.003 (45); Difference 0.007; F-statistic 13.44*** (one-way ANOVA). Text: '0.010 vs. 0.003, p < 0.01'.
contrasts.locator: p. 20, Table 3 Panel C; p. 19 text; p. 34, Table A2

eligibility.reason: MTurk workers randomly assigned to ChatGPT vs Google Search (p. 11); 90 people analyzed after attention-check exclusions (45/45), though rated-quality and diversity outcomes use only the 67 with a valid idea (39/28), still above 50; novelty, appropriateness, and embedding diversity are scored on the submitted ideas (pp. 16-17, Table 3). The comparison arm is an active aid (web search), so contrasts are ai_vs_active.

one_line_finding: Against Google Search, ChatGPT users produced more valid ideas (3.533 vs 1.533, F = 27.65), more novel ideas (0.010 vs -0.057, F = 4.88), less functionally appropriate ideas (0.055 vs 0.213, F = 10.77), and more divergent ideas (0.134 vs 0.123, F = 25.68) (p. 20, Table 3 Panel C).
open_questions: Table 3 Idea Novelty row prints Difference 0.018, but the arm means 0.010 and -0.057 differ by 0.067 (p. 20). Which number is right?

Table 2 (p. 17) gives Idea Novelty mean 0.121 and Functional Appropriateness mean -0.018 (n = 67). The Table 3 arm means weighted by 39 and 28 match the opposite rows (novelty near -0.018, appropriateness near 0.121). Either Table 2 swaps the two rows or Table 3 swaps the labels; Appendix A3/A4 coefficient signs agree with the Table 3 labels.

Table 2 Divergent Thinking row (p. 17) is identical to the Functional Appropriateness row (mean -0.018, SD 0.126), which cannot be right for a 1-minus-cosine measure whose arm means are 0.134 and 0.123. No usable SD for divergent thinking is printed.

No arm SDs or SEs for the total treatment effect are printed; only F-statistics with stars. Appendix A SEs are for the ChatGPT coefficient conditional on a mediator, and the sample size of those models is not stated.
Arm of the 10 excluded participants is not stated; per-arm randomized counts are not given.
Section 5.2.3 says participants who did not use the tools have missing Divergent Thinking, but Table 3 reports it for all 67 with valid ideas.
notes: Process variables (Exploration Depth, Exploration Breadth, Information Volume, Relatedness, Divergency) are measured on prompts or tool responses, not on the ideas, and are not listed. Information Adoption (share of idea sentences copied from tool content, TF-IDF cosine > 0.9; LLM 0.418 (39) vs Search 0.255 (28), F = 3.78*, p. 19 Table 3 Panel B) is scored on ideas but measures reliance, not creativity or diversity, so it is not listed. Tables 4 and 5 (pp. 23-24) regress novelty and appropriateness on Information Adoption x ChatGPT among 49 participants with entropy balancing; these are associations, not randomized contrasts. Randomization check in Table 1 (p. 12): gender share male 0.555 vs 0.733, F = 3.14. Raters and participants were both MTurk workers. Candidate record said assignment was unclear; the PDF states random assignment.
